newsitem.title: UK: Protestant inmates in N.Irish prison protest.
newsitem.headline: Protestant inmates in N.Irish prison protest.

text.p: Convicted pro-British guerrillas tried to burn down two observation towers at the Maze Prison in Northern Ireland on Tuesday in a protest against new security measures.
Prison sources said fires damaged the base of the metal watchtowers in two exercise yards and several prisoners clambered on to the roofs of two cellblocks waving flags and makeshift banners.
Protestant "Loyalists", jailed for crimes in a campaign to preserve Northern Ireland's links with Britain, had earlier refused to cooperate with new search and headcount measures.
The new measures were brought in to tighten security after Irish Republican Army (IRA) extremists serving terms for waging war to end British rule tried to tunnel their way out last month.
Prison sources said staff were withdrawn from the troubled blocks for their own protection and visits by relatives and other privileges were suspended.
Politicians close to banned Loyalist groups said the protest occured because prisoners felt they should not be penalised for the IRA's actions.
The IRA escape plan was foiled when an officer discovered the tunnel. Prison sources said IRA prisoners had cooperated with the new security measures.
